Countdown party mini golf

Ten New York holes · one night · 31 Dec 2026
Carpenter's pack (route C: one carpenter; volunteers paint and dress)

General notes

  1. What this is. Ten mini golf holes for one night (31 Dec 2026), laid on an auditorium floor, built by one carpenter and painted and dressed by volunteers. These drawings show what we want and the key sizes. Please check them, tell us what you'd change, and quote.
  2. Units and setting out. Millimetres. Each hole is drawn with its tee on the left. x is measured along the lane from the outer face of the tee-end rail; y across from the lane centreline. Sheet 2 shows where each hole sits.
  3. Nothing is fixed to the venue floor. Everything sits on the floor (felt or rubber underneath) and is held by its own weight, hidden plates under the playing surface, and sandbags.
  4. Every piece ≤ 2440 long, ≤ 35 kg (two people carry it), fits through the load-in doors (width to be confirmed), and is labelled with hole and part, e.g. H7-R3 (hole 7, rail 3).
  5. Playing rules. Rails stand at least 85 above the playing surface everywhere, including on bevels and raised greens. Any gap between two things a ball can reach is either closed or at least 250. Inside corners are filled. Nowhere can a ball stop out of a putter's reach.
  6. Safety. All edges eased, no sharp corners; screws countersunk; nothing sticks out. Anything over 2 m is braced and ballasted so it can't be pulled over (you confirm). Nothing hangs over a walkway below 2.1 m.
  7. Finish. Deliver paint-ready: filled, sanded, edges rounded. Volunteers prime and paint. Mark faces that show.
  8. Electrics. Low voltage only (24 V LED strip, fitted by our LED lead). Leave a 15 × 15 rebate along the outside bottom edge of every rail for the strip (D1). No mains wiring by the carpenter.
  9. Playing surface. 10 mm carpet grass, needle-punch and white felt, laid by volunteers inside the rails. Allow 10 on top of floors and greens.
  10. Dates. Prototype hole by Fri 4 Dec (we test it); all holes by Fri 18 Dec for a dry-run assembly; install Mon 28 – Tue 29 Dec at the venue.
  11. Still to confirm (by us). Door widths and load-in route; floor finish and flatness; ceiling and rig height for props over 2.4 m; workshop address and hours.
  12. Drawn by the event team with an AI assistant, from the 3D concept. Treat every dimension as a target to check, not a promise.

How a hole goes together

  1. Rails, joined into one closed frame per hole, sit on hidden plates under the playing surface (D1, D4).
  2. A raised green at the cup end, with the rail screwed on top of it and a 1:5 bevel in front (D2, D3, D3b).
  3. Volunteers lay the playing surface inside the rails.
  4. Obstacles screw down through the surface into plates, so nothing can be knocked loose.
  5. Big props stand outside the rails on weighted bases (D6), so nobody leans on them while putting.
  6. The LED strip goes in the rebate on the outside bottom edge of the rail, in the hole's colour.

Where the holes go

Layout v3 from the event plan. The holes keep these footprints in route C. Downtown (holes 10–6) is on one side of the stage runway, Midtown (5–1) on the other; both loop back to the Tee Booth past the runway tip.

Positions are ±1 m until the stage depth and stair positions are measured. We'll set out the holes on site with you on 28 Dec.

Clearances the layout keeps: holes ≥ 1.2 m apart; walkways ≥ 1.2 m; ≥ 1.75 m from the runway side; props over 2 m kept out of the sound desk's sightline.

Floor: finish and flatness to be confirmed. Floor-laid holes take the floor's shape: if it isn't flat, we shim under greens and plates.

Load-in: door widths and route to be confirmed. Pieces ≤ 2440 long.

Design intent for quoting and the prototype. Not engineered. Dimensions in mm; don't scale off the drawing. Check on site.
D1 · RAIL ON THE LANE (section) · 1:2.5
  1. Rail: 45 × 95 dressed timber on edge, straight. Lengths ≤ 2440, each labelled (H7-R3).
  2. 15 × 15 rebate along the outside bottom edge for the LED strip and its cable.
  3. Hidden plate: 6 mm ply 300 × 300 under the rail at every joint, corner and every 1200, reaching 250 inside. Between plates the rail sits on 6 mm rubber strip.
  4. Playing surface (10 mm) laid tight to the rail and over the plate; bevel the plate's inside edge.
  5. Screws up from the plate into the rail.
D2 · RAIL ON A RAISED GREEN (section) · 1:2.5
  1. Rail screwed down through the ply into the edge batten: 75 mm screws, 400 apart.
  2. 12 mm ply top, glued and screwed to the frame.
  3. 45 × 45 batten frame, members ≤ 300 apart, with a batten under every rail.
  4. Surface 10 mm: the green's top is 67 above the floor and the rail still stands 85 above it.
  5. Felt or rubber pads under the frame, so nothing marks the venue floor.
D3 · BEVEL AND CUP (section) · 1:5
  1. Ramp board, 12 mm, at 1:5: 300 long to climb 57.
  2. Tapered battens under the ramp, ≤ 300 apart.
  3. Front edge feathered to nothing (or a tapered threshold strip): no lip for a ball to stop on.
  4. Cup: a 110 hole through the ply; liner = 110 mm PVC drain pipe cut to 57. The ball (Ø43) sits fully below the surface.
  5. Felt disc under the liner, to protect the venue floor.
  6. Frame battens either side of the cup.
D3b · RAIL BESIDE A BEVEL (elevation) · 1:5
  1. Where the surface ramps up, the rail rides up on a tapered packer.
  2. So the sloped rail stays about 85 above the ball the whole way.
  3. Joints at both ends of the sloped piece, over a plate (D4).

D4a · STRAIGHT RAIL JOINT (plan) · 1:10
  1. Rail ends meet over a plate; a dowel or connector bolt keeps them in line and lets the hole come apart.
  2. Plate 300 × 300 × 6 under the surface.
  3. Two screws up through the plate into each rail end.
D4b · CORNER (plan) · 1:10
  1. Butt joint, screwed; label both rails.
  2. Fill every inside corner with a 100 × 100 block so no ball can wedge.
  3. Corner plate underneath.
D5 · TEE END STEP-IN (from the tee) · 1:20
  1. A low rail at the tee end (45 × 45 laid flat, top edge rounded), so players step in rather than over a full rail. LED strip on its outside face too.
D9 · CUT-OUTS AND FLATS (section) · 1:10
  1. Two 6 mm skins glued and pinned to the frame: apple, car front, backdrop, tower, skyline flats.
  2. 45 × 45 frame, members ≤ 600 apart. Single-skin flats (cart front, proscenium, billboards): one 9 or 12 mm sheet with the frame on the back. Fill and sand the edges.
D6 · WEIGHTED PROP BASE · 1:20
  1. Box 600 × 600 × 300, 18 mm ply, screw-on lid.
  2. At least 30 kg ballast (two 15 kg sandbags) per prop up to 2.5 m.
  3. 45° brace from the prop to the box.
  4. Prop screwed into the box. You confirm each prop can't be pulled over.
D7 · TOTEM ×10 · 1:25
  1. Street blades: 6 mm, 600 × 150, green with white letters.
  2. Bullet Ø300 in the hole's colour, number in white.
  3. Post 45 × 45 (or 70 × 70), 2100 tall.
  4. Base box 400 × 400 × 150 with one sandbag.
D8 · PUN SIGN ×10 · 1:25
  1. Board 9 mm, 1150 × 450, black; the pun is painted or LED neon flex (fitted by our LED lead).
  2. Posts 45 × 45, 1700 tall.
  3. Feet 300 × 60 with a sandbag. Stands behind the hole's end rail.

ABike wheel ×5 (free from bike shops), about Ø660, standing across the lane. Centres x 1200 / 2050 / 2900 / 3750 / 4600; y −425 / +425 / 0 / −425 / +425. The outer wheels touch the rail. Axle bolted to a 45 × 45 post (330 tall) behind the wheel; post and cradle screw down through a 6 mm plate under the surface

Please tell us

  1. Your day rate and how many days you estimate.
  2. Which days you're free between 30 Nov and 29 Dec.
  3. What you'd change in these drawings to make it quicker, cheaper or stronger.
  4. Whether you bring your own tools, and what you need from us (space, power, a helper).
  5. Whether you'll buy the materials, and your timber merchant.
  6. Photos of 2–3 things you've built.
